First reasoned review; malware was never executed.

notification-stream-cleanup.cpp (ec6c2c105f04): BENIGN.
The source explicitly calls itself a behavioral reconstruction. wmain writes
Notifycfg.ini with one-pixel WebDAV popup settings; it does not itself fetch or
show the URL. It copies itself to a temporary file and starts that copy with
its own PID and path. The helper waits for the parent to exit, renames the
parent's unnamed NTFS stream, reopens the path and requests deletion. No theft,
backdoor or destructive target is present. Keep the single suspicious ADS
self-deletion trait and the accurate notable config/operation observations.

SSS-decoded.ps1 (ed6a3bbcbe8e): MALICIOUS, Remcos loader.
Read all 124 logical lines and statically extracted both PE images. The script
Base64-decodes its blob, XORs each byte with a cycling UTF-8 key, converts the
result to text and Base64-decodes that text to a 48,128-byte managed assembly.
It reflects FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER and passes aspnet_compiler.exe plus a
537,088-byte native PE. It repeats when the named process is absent.
The managed entry's delegate pipeline creates a suspended child, interprets
PE header fields at offsets 40/52/80/84, allocates memory, copies headers and
sections, rewrites PEB.ImageBaseAddress at saved EBX+8 and saved EAX, updates
thread context and resumes. Unreachable bogus metadata call tokens before
constant-false branches obscure methods. No managed payload was invoked.
Independently traced the native PE's imported calls at 0x41ca00/0x41ca1d/
0x41ca2a: WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext, ResumeThread. At 0x408493 it
builds the CMSTPLUA elevation moniker and calls CoGetObject. Its keylogging
routine at 0x40bf7a starts recording workers; upload routine 0x40a3be reads
files and transfers chunks. The Remcos SETTINGS resource is 597 bytes: the
first byte is the RC4 key length, followed by key and encrypted configuration.
Statically decrypting it recovered controller paticipa.home-webserver.de:9018
and installation/logging settings. No connection was made to that endpoint.
The runtime-path/reflection/PE-data trio alone is not hollowing evidence and
has been removed as a hostile composite. The decoded native hollowing,
elevation and Remcos traits remain. Bare array XOR is direction-neutral
scrambling, and no longer describes a cipher or necessarily a repeating key.

bsoccer.io_chrome.exe (232a36386fa8): MALICIOUS, custom managed spyware.
Disassembled every managed method with dnfile/dncil, resolving metadata tokens.
The namespace is NanoCoreUltimate; it creates several other malware-branded
mutexes and embeds many family names. Those labels do not establish family
identity. Main (RVA 0x2188) invokes surveillance and security-degradation code.
StartKeylogger (0x35e8) installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL. HookCallback (0x3720) reads
key codes and appends timestamps and active-window titles to a buffer.
FlushKeylog (0x37f0) Base64-encodes that buffer with KEYLOG framing and calls
SendToC2 (0x5ff8), which appends it locally and supplies its argument directly
to WebClient.UploadString for the configured HTTP endpoint. ClipboardMonitor
MoveNext (0x3840) reads clipboard text, records changes and calls the same
send helper. Screenshot and selected-file routines also call this helper.
InstallPersistence writes its path into Run keys, copies itself to Startup,
and launches schtasks with onlogon and recurring schedules. USBWorm (0x3efc)
selects ready removable drives, copies its executable and writes autorun.inf.
BypassUAC (0x5624) writes ms-settings shell command and DelegateExecute values,
then launches fodhelper.exe. DeleteShadowCopies (0x4db8) actually launches
vssadmin and wmic deletion commands. Security-service, firewall and policy
routines contain executable launch/write paths, not only labels.
RealEncryption MoveNext (0x4458) enumerates Desktop/TestFolder, reads file
bytes, calls EncryptAES, writes a suffixed replacement and deletes originals.
However, the UTF-8 AES IV initialized by .cctor has only 14 bytes; assigning it
throws before encryption/output/deletion. Existing trait correctly says an
attempt. Independent keylogging/exfiltration, input lockout, persistence and
security degradation establish maliciousness even though encryption fails.
The provided external verdicts were not used as behavioral proof. No trait
changes were needed for this executable's currently reported behavior.
